correctness.rationale: Every arbitrary feasible kernel has Fourier Rayleigh values 1-pbar-u*qbar and 1-pbar-v*qbar. Their minimax and the hub stochasticity bound give the historical exact optimum, attained by the explicit invariant kernel. At spectral error epsilon, scalar crossing gives mean-weight error O(epsilon); the first-harmonic PSD residual is at most epsilon+sqrt[2(mu+epsilon)(1+u/v)epsilon]. Its imaginary coordinate difference controls rim-weight variance via the cycle Poincare inequality; its real part controls spoke-weight error. Each step is an analytic all-m proof. Independently coded finite Jacobi spectral checks passed 22532 assertions for m=4..19, corroborating but not proving the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The known invariant optimal transition weights and minimum SLEM are explicitly credited to Boyd–Diaconis–Parrilo–Xiao Section 5.3.3. The evaluated new claim concerns every noninvariant feasible optimizer and a global explicit near-optimal error bound on all independently weighted spoke and rim edges. Generic symmetry averaging proves existence, not uniqueness or quantitative stability, and generic SDP formalism does not provide the displayed graph-specific constants. value.rationale: Known symmetry averaging cannot distinguish unique from multiple inhomogeneous design implementations. The theorem gives a complete optimizer classification and a quantitative global sensitivity certificate: any nearly fastest chain has individually prescribed edge weights within an explicit O_m(sqrt(epsilon)) RMS bound, under no rotational-invariance hypothesis. This is relevant to interpreting approximate SDP solutions and robustness of network transition design. It does not merely recalculate the known optimal value, and sharpness of the bound is not claimed.
